searchText: Yes (sorry for late reply) Do you think we could start testing on a devnet today? No. We don't have a branch yet The idea would be to use waggle + seacast for proofs? I want to start by iterating on top of current waggle protocol for payload broadcast. TBH I am not yet sure it is feasible to implement full seacast within a week on top of what we currently have in waggle. But we can take some parts of it (e.g. do it without EC in the first iteration if we are not sure about the choice of EC library that we will use across the clients) + we need to adapt it a bit for the proofs objects. For payloads we assumed everyone has the committment from the bid. This is not the case for proofs. For proofs objects I think we need every chunk to have merkle authenticated path + one chunk per peer should have the leanXMSS signature of the root. Or I guess asked differently; can we not just use ai to get something that is a close approximation to what we want i/c of interest I am hoping to have a version of PQ silver with seacast over gossip in the next few days Not sure there’s a strong rationale for why it would take a long time to get a prototype 🤔 would be very interested! I'm also very close to have a SEACAST in prysm. SEACAST has 4 bindings defined: backwards compatible Gossipsub, Waggle, libp2p transport, native QUIC. should be (there is some optimism there 🙂 ) easy to move between these do you have a link? would this be on top of their pq-devnet-0 branch? so that we can already test it on a devnet today? I would rather have something more meaningful in a week. but we can get sloppy implementation today if we really want devnet 0 is a slop cannon so just sendit can someone please remind me of the main objective for the devnet 0? And also what setup do we want to have there? (how many nodes / validators) devnet 0 is where we get something working, that is a close enough approximation of what we want, such that we can draw meaningful conclusions from it so I guess first we get it working, then we go back and clean it up will have a link after some more testing. It is hard to have early release links in todays AI haeavy world without getting much extra overhead added on the way 🙁 can you ping Terence too once you have a link? yes, after a merge (not much conflicts) Okay, from my side I am mostly interested in: 1. Performance: latencies, bandwidth profiles, etc. 2. implementation complexity: I don't want to introduce too complicated protocols if no one will want to actually implement and maintain them First step is to get it working on devnets so we can reason about it end-to-end 😄 <@439032863904628745> Is it possible to get the poc version on a devnet today? lets do that tomorrow, I will prepare some sloppy LH version by then <@412614104222531604> what do we need for the devnet? Would LH branch be enough? yeah I'm working on trying to get the network up today we can swap then one lh image with the waggle supported branch and assuming that we gonna see waggle and gossipsub side by side, we should be good but also not sure if we can sync with lighthouse so swapping an image might break so the plan is: 1. Start the network with gossipsub, collect metrics 2. Swap the images to the waggle version, collect the metrics and compare ? I was gonna recommend to have dual stack (gossipsub and waggle both enabled) so that we can determine which is better (hopefully waggle) is there a reason not to do two separate devnets: one with waggle, one with gossipsub? we can also do that but I don't think we have many cl client impl of waggle yet so we might see totally diff behaviour the main goal of the devnet is testing interop then we need at least two clients with compatible PQ on gossipsub and then compatible PQ on waggle. I think we can do first devnet using <@363800010518822915> 's branch + implement compatible LH branch. Both will work on gossipsub. Then do waggle implementation in the next devnet and compare

I want to start by iterating on top of current waggle protocol for payload broadcast. 

TBH I am not yet sure it is feasible to implement full seacast within a week on top of what we currently have in waggle. But we can take some parts of it (e.g. do it without EC in the first iteration if we are not sure about the choice of EC library that we will use across the clients)

+ we need to adapt it a bit for the proofs objects. For payloads we assumed everyone has the committment from the bid. This is not the case for proofs. For proofs objects I think we need every chunk to have merkle authenticated path + one chunk per peer should have the leanXMSS signature of the root.
